chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Udhayfir from Umar ibn Yazid from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you slaughter your Udhiyah (sacrificial animal), shave your head, perform ghusl, trim your nails, and take from your mustache." And whoever deliberately leaves shaving or shortens [the hair] until he performs Hajj, a sheep's blood (dam) is obligatory upon him. And whoever does that forgetfully, there is nothing upon him; he should shorten [his hair] and then repeat Tawaf and Sa'i. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.أُضْحِيَّةٌ: Sacrificial animal slaughtered during Hajj or Eid al-Adha
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: Blood of a sheep (a specific ritual penalty)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual requirements and penalties for shaving or shortening hair during Hajif the Udhiyah sacrifice?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific acts of grooming—shaving the head, ghusl, nail trimming, and mustache cutting—performed upon slaughtering the Udhiyah, linking physical purification with ritual completion. It establishes a clear jurisprudential distinction where deliberate neglect incurs a financial penalty (dam of a sheep), while forgetful omission requires only the repetition of Tawaf and Sa'i after shortening the hair, reflecting the Shia emphasis on intentionality in ritual obligations.
